<!-- With my growing interests in pure mathematics, I changed my first-year math sequence from applied to honors sequence in the Winter Quarter. That means I did not know how to speak the basic language of mathematics, not even the principle of induction. Consequently, I initially struggled a lot in the course. However, Yakov Eliashberg, who was the instructor, would (even while being, understandingly, a little grumpy) hold extra personal office hours, give out additional problems. While I ended up with a B+, I left the course having fallen in love with mathematics more than ever.

On the last night of bootcamp for my mandatory service, the drill instructor made an announcement: that he would have succeeded as a drill instructor if he could reach to one trainee by heart. 

That is why whether I teach ten, a hundred, or a thousand students, I will teach with the same care and diligence for the sake of those who is willing to learn—even if it might be a single student. If I can reach that one student, I will consider myself to have succeeded as an educator. -->
